common_name: Yaezaki Farfugium (Jitsuko's Star, Double-Flowered Leopard Plant)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade; Yaezaki (trade name Jitsuko's Star) is a double-flowered leopard plant selection, distinct from the more common single-flowered farfugium cultivars already grown for their bold, glossy foliage.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in light to full shade; Yaezaki is grown as much for its glossy, rounded, leathery evergreen leaves as for its flowers, giving the shade garden a bold, almost tropical texture that contrasts well with finer-textured ferns and hostas. In fall it produces double, fully ruffled yellow daisy-like flowers on tall stems above the foliage, a showier display than the simple single flowers of most farfugium cultivars. Give it protection from direct afternoon sun and hard freezes, since the large leaves scorch in strong sun and can be damaged by hard frost, though the crown typically survives and resprouts in zone 8 with adequate mulch. Slugs and snails are drawn to the tender new growth, so watch for damage in damp conditions.

common_name: Applecourt Japanese Painted Fern (Crested Painted Fern)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring once new growth is visible; Applecourt is a crested selection of Japanese painted fern, chosen for frond tips that split into decorative fan-like crests in addition to the species' typical silver, green, and burgundy coloring.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in dappled to full shade; Applecourt is a crested selection of Japanese painted fern, meaning the tips of the fronds and pinnae split into small, decorative fan-shaped crests, giving the plant a more ornate texture than the straight species while retaining its signature silver, green, and burgundy frond coloring. The best color develops with some morning light, but foliage will fade or scorch in afternoon sun. Divide congested clumps every few years in early spring to keep the planting vigorous and to share starts. Remove spent fronds in late winter before new fiddleheads emerge, and protect newly planted divisions from slugs, which are drawn to the tender new growth.

common_name: Crispa Whiteside Broad Buckler Fern (Crested Heirloom Fern)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in consistently moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial to full shade; Crispa Whiteside is a historic crested selection of the broad buckler fern, discovered by Victorian fern collector Robert Whiteside and holding a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial to full shade; Crispa Whiteside is a dwarf, tightly crested selection of the broad buckler fern, with each frond tip and pinna dividing into dense, ruffled crests that give the whole plant a frilly, congested texture quite different from the airy, open form of the straight species. It is a historic cultivar, discovered by the Victorian-era fern collector Robert Whiteside and reintroduced to cultivation in the mid-20th century, and it holds the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for garden performance. Keep soil consistently moist and mulch with leaf litter to mimic its woodland-floor origins, since it will not tolerate prolonged dry spells. Divide congested clumps in early spring if needed, and remove old fronds before new growth emerges to keep the crested form looking its best.

common_name: Vision in Red Astilbe (Dark Red-Plumed Bronze-Leaved Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in consistently moist, organically rich soil in partial shade; Vision in Red is part of the Dutch Vision series of astilbe chinensis hybrids, bred for compact size and unusually good drought tolerance compared to most astilbe, though it still performs best with reliable moisture in a Gulf South summer.

directions: Plant crowns so the top of the rhizome sits 1-2 inches below the soil surface in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Vision in Red bears dense, dark purplish-red plumes over bronze-tinted green foliage on a compact plant, one of the more richly colored selections in the popular Vision series of astilbe chinensis hybrids. Like other Vision-series astilbe, it is somewhat more tolerant of dry spells than older astilbe cultivars, though it still performs best and blooms most heavily with consistent moisture through summer. Leave the dried plumes standing through fall and winter for ornamental interest, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous bloom.
